title: Rolling Over Equity Futures: A Study in Four Countries
one_line: For ES (and FTSE, Nifty, A50) 2016 expirations, ~90% of calendar-spread volume falls in the last 5 days before expiry (ES peak on day 12 of a 15-day window); ES spread volatility rises through the roll window, so rolling earlier lowers risk; spreads stay within a 0.5% no-arbitrage band.

findings.statement: Spread volume > 10% of futures volume from roll-window day 8-11; peaks 40-70% on days 12-14.
Volatility-minimizing roll beats even and stack rolls in US, India, China.

why.pattern: Execution mechanics of the quarterly roll.

tradable_edge: No strategy. Backtest hygiene: our continuous ES series should switch on volume (as the data already does) and roll-week days can be flagged as a split.
data_fit: ES 1-min Dec 2013 → Sep 2026, NQ 1-min Jul 2021 → Sep 2026 (2024+ protected in the backtest project).
